imp.name: implied
imp.text: The instruction needs no operand; it is part of the instruction itself (for example `INX`). The instruction is one byte long.

acc.name: accumulator
acc.text: The instruction works on register `A`. Write `A` or leave the operand out (`ASL A`).

imm.name: immediate
imm.text: The number is part of the instruction: `LDA #$05` loads the number 5. The `#` tells it apart from an address.

zp.name: zero page
zp.text: An address from `$00` to `$FF` (the first page of memory). Shorter and faster than an absolute address.

zpx.name: zero page,X
zpx.text: A zero-page address plus `X`. It wraps around without leaving the page (`$FF,X` with `X=5` gives `$04`).

zpy.name: zero page,Y
zpy.text: A zero-page address plus `Y`. Only possible with `LDX` and `STX`.

abs.name: absolute
abs.text: A full 16-bit address (`$0000` to `$FFFF`). In the instruction the low byte comes first, then the high byte.

abx.name: absolute,X
abx.text: A 16-bit address plus `X`. Reading instructions take one extra cycle when a page boundary is crossed.

aby.name: absolute,Y
aby.text: A 16-bit address plus `Y`. Reading instructions take one extra cycle when a page boundary is crossed.

ind.name: indirect
ind.text: Only with `JMP`: the address in the instruction points to two bytes that together form the jump target. (The real 6502 has a bug here: if the address is `$xxFF`, the high byte is read from `$xx00`. The emulator reproduces it.)

izx.name: indexed indirect
izx.text: `($nn,X)`: `X` is added to `$nn`, and the address of the operand is stored there (two bytes in the zero page). Selects an entry from a table of pointers.

izy.name: indirect indexed
izy.text: `($nn),Y`: `$nn` and `$nn+1` hold an address, and `Y` is added to it. The most common kind of pointer access.

rel.name: relative
rel.text: Only for branches: an offset from −128 to +127 bytes, measured from the next instruction. In the source you write a label.

LDA.name: Load accumulator
LDA.text: Copies a number or the contents of a memory cell into `A`. `Z` becomes 1 if the value is 0; `N` becomes 1 if bit 7 is set.

STA.name: Store accumulator
STA.text: Writes `A` to a memory cell. Does not change any flags. Written into the screen area (`$0200` to `$05FF`), it colours a pixel.

TXS.name: Transfer X to stack pointer
TXS.text: Copies `X` to the stack pointer `SP`. The only transfer instruction that sets no flags.

PHA.name: Push accumulator
PHA.text: Puts `A` on the stack (`$0100` to `$01FF`) and decreases `SP` by 1.

PLA.name: Pull accumulator
PLA.text: Increases `SP` by 1 and takes the top value from the stack into `A`. Sets `N` and `Z`.

PHP.name: Push processor status
PHP.text: Puts the status register `P` on the stack. The flag `B` is stored as 1.

PLP.name: Pull processor status
PLP.text: Takes the status register from the stack. All flags take the stored values.

ADC.name: Add with carry
ADC.text: Adds the operand and the carry flag to `A`. Before a single addition, clear the carry with `CLC`. If the result exceeds 255, the low byte stays in `A` and `C` becomes 1. With the decimal flag set (`SED`) the instruction works with two-digit decimal numbers (BCD).

SBC.name: Subtract with carry
SBC.text: Subtracts the operand from `A`, and one more if the carry is clear. Before a single subtraction, set the carry with `SEC`. `C = 0` afterwards means the result was negative.

AND.name: Bitwise AND
AND.text: Combines `A` with the operand bit by bit: a result bit is 1 if both bits are 1. With a mask you hide bits.

ORA.name: Bitwise OR
ORA.text: A result bit is 1 if at least one of the two bits is 1. Sets bits.

EOR.name: Bitwise exclusive OR
EOR.text: A result bit is 1 if exactly one of the two bits is 1. Flips bits.

BIT.name: Test bits
BIT.text: Tests `A` against a memory cell without changing `A`: `Z` is 1 if `A ∧ value` is zero; `N` and `V` copy bits 7 and 6 of the memory cell.

ASL.name: Arithmetic shift left
ASL.text: Shifts all bits one place to the left; a 0 comes in on the right, the bit pushed out of position 7 lands in the carry. Doubles the number.

LSR.name: Logical shift right
LSR.text: Shifts all bits one place to the right; a 0 comes in on the left, the bit pushed out of position 0 lands in the carry. Halves the number (rounded down). `N` is always 0.

ROL.name: Rotate left
ROL.text: Like `ASL`, but the old carry comes in on the right (rotation through the carry).

ROR.name: Rotate right
ROR.text: Like `LSR`, but the old carry comes in on the left.

INC.name: Increment memory
INC.text: Increases the contents of a memory cell by 1. From 255 it goes to 0 (without carry).

DEC.name: Decrement memory
DEC.text: Decreases the contents of a memory cell by 1. From 0 it goes to 255.

INX.name: Increment X
INX.text: Increases `X` by 1. From 255 it goes to 0 and sets `Z`.

DEX.name: Decrement X
DEX.text: Decreases `X` by 1. From 0 it goes to 255.

CMP.name: Compare accumulator
CMP.text: Computes `A − value` without changing `A` and only sets flags: `Z` = equal, `C` = `A` is greater or equal, `N` = bit 7 of the difference.

BCC.name: Branch if carry clear
BCC.text: Branches if `C = 0`. After a comparison: less than (unsigned).

BCS.name: Branch if carry set
BCS.text: Branches if `C = 1`. After a comparison: greater or equal (unsigned).

BEQ.name: Branch if equal
BEQ.text: Branches if `Z = 1`, that is if the last result was 0 or both values in a comparison were equal.

BMI.name: Branch if minus
BMI.text: Branches if `N = 1`, that is if bit 7 of the last result is set.

JMP.name: Jump
JMP.text: Sets the program counter to the target address, unconditionally. Reaches all of memory. With `($nnnn)` it reads the target from memory.

JSR.name: Jump to subroutine
JSR.text: Pushes the address of the last byte of its own instruction onto the stack and jumps to the target. `RTS` returns to the instruction after it.

RTS.name: Return from subroutine
RTS.text: Pulls the return address from the stack, adds 1 and jumps there.

RTI.name: Return from interrupt
RTI.text: Pulls first the flags, then the return address from the stack. Not needed in this environment because there are no interrupts.

BRK.name: Break
BRK.text: On a real 6502, `BRK` pushes the address after the instruction and the flags onto the stack and jumps through the vector at `$FFFE`. In this environment **`BRK` stops the program**; that is how you end one. The byte `00` is also found everywhere memory is empty.

NOP.name: No operation
NOP.text: Does nothing except use up time (2 cycles). Useful as a placeholder or for waiting.

CLC.name: Clear carry
CLC.text: Sets the carry flag to 0. Belongs in front of every single addition.

CLD.name: Clear decimal mode
CLD.text: Sets the decimal flag to 0; `ADC` and `SBC` calculate in binary again.

CLI.name: Clear interrupt disable
CLI.text: Sets flag `I` to 0. Has no effect in this environment.

SEC.name: Set carry
SEC.text: Sets the carry flag to 1. Belongs in front of every single subtraction.

SED.name: Set decimal mode
SED.text: Sets the decimal flag; `ADC` and `SBC` then work with two-digit decimal numbers (BCD), for example `$19 + $28 = $47`.

SEI.name: Set interrupt disable
SEI.text: Sets flag `I` to 1. Has no effect in this environment.
